headline: Saudi slips on a Houthi strike claim at Ras Tanura while the UAE rises on bank consolidation; oil rebounds above $90 and US core inflation hits a three-year high
analysis: Wednesday: TASI -0.63% to 9,914, Abu Dhabi +0.48% to 9,920, Dubai +0.44% to 6,388, Qatar -0.27% to 10,024 (TradingView). The Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, and threatened Red Sea ports; a person with knowledge told Reuters the refinery was attacked, Saudi authorities did not comment, and a separate attack on a Riyadh tower injured 11 (Business Recorder; Nation Thailand; Investing.com). Brent's February contract settled $90.91 (+2.4%), back above $90 for the first time since 17-Nov, helped by three vessels struck near Hormuz and pre-holiday covering despite a US crude build; OPEC+ meets Sunday (Investing.com; Nation Thailand). In the US, October core PCE rose to 3.3% y/y (3.2% expected) and Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3%, so a 25 bp hike on 9-Dec is priced with January in play (Kotak Neo). DIB agreed an all-share purchase of Emirates Islamic, the UAE's biggest Islamic-bank deal in years. Our replica benchmark -0.19%, the fund -0.12%.
positioning: Defensive, low beta: Saudi -9.0 pts, Qatar +2.6, Kuwait +1.7, UAE neutral, cash 4.7%. Oil names at index weight; UAE tilt now in ADIB, DEWA, du and telecoms rather than DIB's merger. +74 bps since launch, about half from dividend income.
risks: A US-Iran deal sparking a relief rally in high-beta Saudi names we under-own; confirmed damage at Ras Tanura lifting oil and Aramco; a 50 bp Fed hike; more DMTT disclosures at our Saudi overweights.
watch: Ras Tanura damage reports; OPEC+ 29-Nov; Brent vs $95; TASI vs 9,800; Elm test 30-Nov; DIB GA circular; Fed 9-Dec.

horizon: 1-3 months; reviewed weekly on foreign flows
headline: TASI -0.6% to 9,914 as banks lead the fall after the Ras Tanura claim; 1.2% above our 9,800 rebuild level
analysis: Banks did the damage: Al Rajhi -1.2% to 60.35, Alinma -0.4%, Bank Albilad -1.0% to 19.83 (RSI 30), Ma'aden -1.2% to 55.40, SABIC -1.2% to 47.42, while Aramco held at 26.26 (-0.2%) and Tawuniya rose 1.4% (TradingView; Business Recorder). TASI is 3.0% below its 50-day (10,222) and 8.3% below its 200-day (10,811). A claimed strike on the kingdom's largest refinery and an attack in Riyadh keep the conflict premium on Saudi assets, not just on oil. Our names: STC -0.4% to 40.40, Jarir -1.0% to 15.74 (back under its 200-day), SAL -1.3% to 164.50 (just above its 50-day), Elm -0.4% to 589.50, Nahdi -2.0% to 87.65, Marafiq +1.2% to 45.44. No Tadawul foreign-flow data since the week to 5-Nov.
positioning: Underweight ~9.0 pts (limit 10). Aramco, Al Rajhi, Alinma, Luberef at index weight; SABIC, ACWA, Ma'aden underweight. Overweight STC (+1.4), Jarir, SAL, Elm, Bupa, Almarai, Habib; off-index Marafiq and Nahdi.
risks: A ceasefire rally in names we do not own; DMTT or tariff costs at our overweights; little room under the 10-pt limit if TASI breaks 9,800 and we want to add to the underweight.
watch: Ras Tanura damage; TASI vs 9,800 and its 50-day (10,222); Elm vs its 200-day (620) on 30-Nov; flow print; DMTT disclosures.

headline: Abu Dhabi +0.5%, Dubai +0.4%: DIB agrees to buy Emirates Islamic for 3.49bn new shares; Emaar +2.7%
analysis: DIB will issue 3,486,284,330 new shares to Emirates NBD (0.642 per Emirates Islamic share) for 100% of Emirates Islamic; ENBD will own 32.5% of the enlarged bank and combined assets reach ~AED 585bn vs DIB's AED 427bn. No valuation, earnings or accretion figures were given; a General Assembly, CBUAE and CMA approvals are needed (The National; Gulf News; Edge Consultancy). DIB rose 1.6% to 8.92 (RSI 86, ~3x average volume). Emaar +2.7% to 12.98, ADIB +1.8% to 25.04, ADNOC L&S +2.4% to 7.65, Salik +2.4%, SIB +3.4%; IHC +0.2% to 312.60 (RSI 20); e& +0.4% to 23.70 (RSI 73); du -0.3% to 13.68 (TradingView).
positioning: Neutral (+0.1 pt). Maximum underweight IHC (-4.2). Overweight ADIB (+1.8), DEWA (+1.2), du (+1.1), Talabat, ADNOC L&S (+0.8), e&, Emaar; DIB now at index weight; off-index AD Ports and TECOM.
risks: DIB's terms prove accretive and it keeps running without us; an IHC rebound from RSI 20; attacks on shipping off the UAE coast.
watch: DIB GA circular; IHC; Emaar Development offer to 10-Dec; Fed 9-Dec for property.

Our Qatar names fell 0.62% vs 0.43% for the slice. No LNG disruption reported; three vessels were struck near Hormuz this week (UKMTO via Investing.com).
positioning: Overweight ~2.6 pts: QIB, Ooredoo, QFLS, Vodafone Qatar, QIIB, Nebras, Barwa, Milaha; Masraf Al Rayan and Dukhan at index weight. Underweight Industries Qatar and Mesaieed.
risks: An attack on LNG facilities; friction between Iran and the mediator; Milaha losing its shipping premium.
watch: Milaha vs its 200-day; any LNG disruption; OPEC+ and gas prices.

headline: KFH +0.5% to 770 fils, at its 200-day; Zain slips under 570
analysis: KFH +0.5% to 770 fils (50-day 762, 200-day 770, RSI 60), Boubyan -0.5% to 656, Zain -0.7% to 569 (below its 200-day 584), Mabanee +0.5% to 971, Humansoft +0.3% to 2,196 (RSI 38) (TradingView). Our Kuwait names +0.25% vs +0.27% for the slice; Kuwait added 0.8 bps through the overweight on a down day for the region. No new strike on Kuwait reported.
positioning: Overweight ~1.7 pts: KFH (+1.4), Zain (+0.8), off-index Humansoft (+0.8); Boubyan below index weight.
risks: Strikes on Kuwaiti infrastructure; low beta lags a relief rally; a long spell of oil below $90 slows government spending.
